title: Rules and good advice
grammar: Modal verbs: can, must, mustn't, should, have to

scene.speaker: nova
scene.bubble: Read about Nadia's first workshop, learn the modal verbs, then write the rules for your own team.
scene.intro: The Inspiring Nordic project has its first Trades workshop this week, and workshops need rules to keep everyone safe. In this unit you read about Nadia's first day in the workshop, you learn the modal verbs we use for rules and advice — must, mustn't, should, have to and can — and then you write the rules for your own team. Good rules don't stop the fun; they keep it safe. Let's get started.

data.author: nadia
data.title: My first workshop
data.text:
Today we had our first Trades workshop for the Inspiring Nordic project, and I was so excited — but also a little nervous. There are so many rules!

Before we started, our teacher explained them. You must wear safety glasses and closed shoes. You mustn't run near the machines, and you mustn't touch the tools without asking. You should always listen carefully and put your things away at the end.

At first the rules seemed difficult, but our teacher said something clever: “The rules are not here to stop the fun. They are here to keep the fun safe.” After that, I felt much braver.

I can tell you it was a great class. I built a small wooden box, I helped Liam with his, and I followed every rule. Next week we have to bring our own ideas for the poster. I can't wait!

data.title: Modal verbs: rules and advice
data.intro: We use modal verbs to talk about rules, advice and ability. After a modal verb we use the base verb with no 'to'.

examples.text: You should ask if you're not sure.

rules: must = it is necessary; mustn't = it is not allowed (prohibited).
After a modal, use the base verb with no to: You should ask (not to ask). We say have to + verb.

items.sentence: You ___ wear a helmet on a bike. It's the law.
You ___ run in the lab. It's dangerous.
You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
We ___ bring our own ideas next week.
It's Saturday, so we ___ get up early.

activities.title: Listening — the safety talk. Write ONE word in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voz: la profesora (Miss Vega), tono claro dando reglas.
data.script: Good morning, Grade 6. Before our first Trades workshop, here are some important rules. You must wear closed shoes in the workshop, and you mustn't run near the machines. You should always listen to the teacher and put on safety glasses. You can ask questions at any time, but you have to keep your table tidy. If we follow these rules, everyone stays safe. Thank you!

activities.title: Speaking — give the rules. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: In pairs, give three rules for a place you know: your classroom, the library or your home. Use must, mustn't and should. Model: “In the library you must be quiet. You mustn't eat. You should return your books.” Then record your rules.

homework.prompt: Write five rules for your Inspiring Nordic Trades team. Use must, mustn't and should, for example: 'We must clean our table.' 'We mustn't shout.' 'We should help each other.' Capital letters and full stops!
